_comment: AUTHORED OWNERSHIP DECISIONS for MSF30322. Every family in families/ACI-MSF30322.families.json appears exactly once below.
_deliveredNote: 25 units across 8 clusters over 92 weeks. Cluster 1 WHS and workplace fundamentals, 2 measurement and documentation, 3 tools machines and joints, 4 timber and materials, 5 drawing and CAD, 6 cabinetry fabrication, 7 installation and on-site work, 8 customer service. WARNING: MSFGN2001 in Cluster 2 is SUPERSEDED on training.gov.au - see openItems in the course record.

topics.name: Reporting hazards, incidents and injuries
topics.rationale: Both construction WHS units sit in Cluster 1. CPCWHS1001 is the White Card statutory induction and is the first thing a learner does; CPCCWHS2001 follows it in the same cluster with the organisational procedure.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCWHS2001 teaches only the delta - the employer's own procedure, the register, and the notifiable-incident duty owed to the regulator.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer identifies a hazard by its potential to cause harm, not by whether harm occurred, and states who it is reported to, how, and within what time. It distinguishes a hazard from an incident from an injury, and names the record each one goes into.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Workplace health and safety procedures in a furniture workshop
topics.rationale: Six units name workplace WHS procedures. The construction WHS units in Cluster 1 own the LEGAL frame; MSFFM2013 Use furniture making hand and power tools, first in Cluster 3, owns the workshop-floor procedure - machine guarding, isolation, housekeeping, dust - because that is the first unit where a learner picks up a tool.
topics.teachingRule: Later units name the procedure that governs their own operation and the specific risk it controls. None of them restate the general duty, which belongs to Cluster 1.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the workshop procedure that governs the machine or task, the guarding and isolation it requires, and the reporting path when something is unsafe.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Personal protective equipment for furniture and cabinetry work
topics.rationale: Seven units name PPE. Every one of them names the SAME equipment for a different operation - eye, hearing, respiratory and hand protection against the same timber dust, noise and blade hazards. Teaching it seven times teaches nothing new six of those times.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM2013 teaches selection, fit, inspection and care once. Every later unit states which items its operation requires and why, in a line, and is assessed on WEARING them rather than on knowing what they are.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer selects PPE against the specific hazard of the tool in use - noise, dust, projectile, chemical - states how it is fitted and checked, and what maintenance and storage it needs.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Reporting machinery faults and material defects
topics.rationale: A fault report is one procedure - tag out, report, do not use. MSFFM2016 Join solid timber is the earliest of the three units in Cluster 3 to require it.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM2018 and MSFFM3042 identify the faults and defects specific to their own machines and materials. The reporting procedure itself is cited.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states how a fault or defect is identified, who it is reported to and by what record, and that the machine or material is taken out of use until cleared.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Workplace records, reporting and the legislation behind them
topics.rationale: Two families - record keeping requirements, and the legislative requirements attaching to work activities - are one topic in Cluster 1: what has to be written down, and which instrument requires it. MSMSUP106 Work in a team is delivered in Cluster 1 and carries organisational procedure as its own subject matter.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFF2012 records its own surface-preparation results to that format. MSFFDM4002 identifies the specific legislation bearing on production processes, and does not restate what legislation is.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer identifies the record the activity requires, states what must be captured and how long it is kept, and names the legislative or organisational requirement behind it.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Characteristics, features and components of cabinetry products
topics.rationale: MSFFM3041 Determine and document requirements for cabinetry installation is delivered first in Cluster 6 and must name the components before it can specify them. MSFFM3042 Fabricate cabinetry then builds them.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM3042 teaches how each component is MADE - the machining, the edge treatment, the assembly - not what it is called or what it is for.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer names the components of the cabinet and states the function and material of each, and how they assemble into the finished product.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Door and drawer systems, and their alignment
topics.rationale: MSFKB2003 Prepare for cabinetry installation, in Cluster 6, owns the hardware - hinge types, runner types, how each is specified and set out. MSFFM3043 Install cabinetry, in Cluster 7, owns adjusting them true on site, which is a different skill and is genuinely new.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM3043 does not re-teach hardware selection. It teaches the three-way adjustment and the sequence for bringing a run of doors into line.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer selects the hinge or runner system for the door or drawer, states the adjustment each provides, and describes how alignment and consistent gapping are achieved and checked.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Reading the building: wall and floor construction and out-of-square conditions
topics.rationale: A cabinetmaker measures the room before making anything, and again before fixing anything. MSFFM3041 in Cluster 6 owns it because the survey is what its documentation is FOR.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM3043 applies the scribing and packing techniques that an out-of-square condition demands, and cites MSFFM3041 for how the condition was identified.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer measures the opening rather than trusting the drawing, identifies out-of-square, out-of-plumb and uneven floor conditions, and states how the installation is scribed or packed to accommodate them.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Statutory planning regulations affecting cabinetry installation
topics.rationale: Local and state planning requirements are a single body of regulation. It is explained where a learner first has to check it - at the documentation stage, in MSFFM3041.
topics.teachingRule: MSFFM3043 confirms the approval is in place before installing and names the consequence of installing without it. It does not re-explain the planning system.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer names the planning or building requirement affecting the installation, states what it requires, and identifies the approval or certificate involved.
